content.title: Short-Term Rental Permit
content.summary: A short-term rental (STR) is a unit rented for less than 30 nights, with a minimum stay of 2 nights. The City of Arvada requires both a short-term rental permit and a business license to operate an STR within the city, with updated rules effective May 1, 2026.

steps.title: Review STR Requirements
steps.text: Read the City of Arvada Land Development Code and the Short-term rental application info page to understand the requirements for operating an STR.

steps.title: Apply for STR Permit and Business License
steps.text: Submit applications for both a short-term rental permit and a business license to legally operate an STR in Arvada.

steps.title: Comply with Inspections and Enforcement
steps.text: Follow the rules and prepare for inspections as outlined on the Operating a short-term rental page. Maintain compliance to avoid penalties.

required_documents.name: Short Term Rental Annual Log
required_documents.description: A log documenting STR activity as required by the City.

required_documents.name: Good Neighbor Guide
required_documents.description: Guide outlining expectations for STR operators to maintain good relations with neighbors.

required_documents.name: Model Brochure for Contact Information and Local Points of Interest
required_documents.description: A brochure template for providing guests with local information and contact details.

faqs.q: What are the main changes taking effect May 1, 2026?
faqs.a: The City updated the ordinance to strengthen enforcement measures, adjust the number of STR permits an individual can have at one time, and clarify who can hold an STR permit.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to operate a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Yes, both a short-term rental permit and a business license are required to operate an STR within the City of Arvada.

faqs.q: How many short-term rentals can one owner operate, and how many days a year can it be rented?
faqs.a: Refer to the City of Arvada Land Development Code and the Short-term rental application info page for specific limits.

faqs.q: Who can operate a short-term rental?
faqs.a: The updated ordinance clarifies the rules around who can hold an STR permit.

faqs.q: Can I operate a short-term rental out of a townhome/condo or accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?
faqs.a: Refer to the City of Arvada Land Development Code for regulations regarding STRs in townhomes, condos, or ADUs.

faqs.q: What is the process for obtaining a short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: Information about the application process is available on the Short-term rental application info page.

faqs.q: Do I also need a business license?
faqs.a: Yes, a business license is required in addition to the STR permit.

faqs.q: What are the fees associated with holding a short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: Fees are detailed on the Short-term rental application info page.

faqs.q: If I hold a short-term rental permit, what are my obligations to maintain the permit?
faqs.a: Obligations include compliance with inspections and enforcement measures as outlined by the City.

faqs.q: Will my short-term rental be subject to inspections?
faqs.a: Yes, inspections are part of the enforcement process.

faqs.q: I want to install a sports court, does it need a permit?
faqs.a: Refer to the City's building permit requirements for sports courts.
Building permits depend on the type of work; consult the City's building department.

faqs.q: What penalties could I be subject to if my STR is found to be in violation of the City's code?
faqs.a: Penalties are outlined in the City's enforcement policies.

faqs.q: My property currently has no active stays. Can I still list it on rental sites while I wait for my permit?
faqs.a: Refer to the City's regulations regarding active listings and permit status.

faqs.q: What counts as an "active listing" if I'm not accepting guests?
faqs.a: Definitions of active listings are provided in the City's STR regulations.

faqs.q: How can I raise concerns about STRs in my neighborhood?
faqs.a: Use the Report a short-term rental concern page to raise issues.
